explanation: Bisect the value range. Count values in the lower half; if its population exceeds its capacity, a duplicate lies there, otherwise one lies in the upper half.
correctness: The maintained interval contains more array occurrences than distinct possible values after discarding the other half when safe. Pigeonhole counting therefore keeps a duplicate until a single value remains.
walkthrough: For [1,3,4,2,3], candidate values are 1..4. The lower half 1..2 contains two entries, fitting its two slots, so continue in 3..4. Value 3 alone appears twice but has only one available slot; narrowing finishes at 3. Every pass reads the same unchanged input.
